label: Audience modelling
summary: Audience modelling is the practice of understanding your audience in terms of experience level, required jargon, task execution, and mental model, rather than relying on superficial persona details. In Maaike's work it functions as a corrective to expert-centric writing, where a writer defaults to their own perspective and level of understanding instead of the audience's. It is treated as an active, ongoing part of the content design process rather than a one-off research step.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike frames audience modelling as one of the core checks in her content quality audit, specifically as a counter to the pitfall of writing from your own vantage point. She emphasises knowing your audience's experience level, jargon, and mental model, and recommends involving people from your actual audience at every phase of the content design process. The point is not abstract persona work but making sure the content connects at the right level for the people who will actually use it.
open_questions: What specific methods or techniques does Maaike use to model audience experience level and mental model in practice?
How does audience modelling interact with stakeholder expectations when the two are in tension?
